author: human
request:
Feature request: the vet list answers "which specialties does this vet hold",
but staff also ask the inverse — "which vets hold this specialty". Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- A read-only specialty view of the existing directory is in scope; managing
  veterinarians or specialties stays out of scope as before (non-goal NG-2
  is unchanged).
- The page is reachable by its URL alone: no navigation entry and no link
  from another page is part of this request. A visible entry point may come
  as a follow-up request.

Add a specialty directory page:

- GET /specialties.html lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored
  name, each with the veterinarians holding it.
- Each veterinarian is shown by full name: first name, then last name (for
  example "Helen Leary").
- A veterinarian holding no specialty appears under no specialty; the page
  lists specialties, not the full vet roster.
- All specialties render on one page — no pagination.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the vet feature package and adds no module, pattern, or dependency. Three existing patterns carry it: Repository for a lookup value (PetTypeRepository is the precedent for a per-lookup-type repository sorted by name), Value object for the read projection, and Web controller for a second GET route on VetController. The one adjustment to durable memory is the Contracts table, which now names SpecialtyRepository and SpecialtyDirectory, and carries REQ-SPECIALTYDIRECTORY-001 against Vet, Specialty and VetController (docs/system-design.md #contracts). The acceptance criterion that a specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed forces the read to start from the specialties table rather than from the veterinarian collection: Vet.getSpecialties() can never yield an unheld specialty, so a new SpecialtyRepository is the minimum addition. Veterinarians come from the existing cached VetRepository.findAll(), whose EAGER specialty mapping already survives the disabled open-in-view. Grouping lives in SpecialtyDirectory, not in the controller: the architecture-principles Web controller row admits no business rule, and its note states the existing controller deviation does not extend to new rules. SpecialtyDirectory imports no framework type and is unit-testable without Spring, which is the shape testing-principles asks for. Basis is grep plus direct reads of the vet package, VetControllerTests, CacheConfiguration, fragments/layout.html and I18nPropertiesSyncTest; the IDE oracle is not connected, so the resolution claim rests on those reads.
integration_points: VetController gains a GET /specialties.html handler taking no request parameter and returning the view name vets/specialtyList; the existing /vets.html paging handler and the /vets serialization route are untouched
VetController gains a second constructor argument, SpecialtyRepository; VetControllerTests must supply it under @WebMvcTest(VetController.class) or the context fails to start

SpecialtyRepository extends Repository<Specialty, Integer> with one @Query method ordering by name, matching VetRepository's narrow-interface style in the same package rather than PetTypeRepository's JpaRepository; the narrow interface is hand-doubleable in tests without Mockito

templates/vets/specialtyList.html reuses fragments/layout with a menu key that matches no navigation entry, so the fixed four-item navbar gains nothing and highlights nothing — this is how the no-navigation-entry non-goal is honored
the seeded H2/MySQL/Postgres data.sql files already carry the specialties table and the vet_specialties join table; no schema or seed change is needed

patterns.description: lookup-value repository returning its rows in name order via an explicit @Query — the shape SpecialtyRepository copies
handler that populates the model and returns a view name; the specialty handler mirrors it without the pagination helper
table template driven by a model list, with every literal resolved through #{} keys
Value object (In force) is the pattern SpecialtyDirectory matches: immutable, defensive copies, equality by value, no framework import

risks.risk: Persisted types override neither equals nor hashCode, so Specialty instances compare by object identity. The specialties come from SpecialtyRepository while the veterinarians come from the @Cacheable VetRepository.findAll(), potentially a different persistence context, so the same specialty row can arrive as two distinct instances. Grouping by object equality would silently list every specialty as unheld.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyDirectory groups by Specialty.getId(). Recorded in docs/system-design.md under the Contracts invariants paragraph. A test that builds the two sides as separate instances of the same identifier pins it.

risks.risk: Annotating the specialty read @Cacheable would fail at runtime: CacheConfiguration creates only the vets cache through the JCache API, and an undeclared cache name has no configuration.
risks.mitigation: SpecialtyRepository carries no cache annotation. Recorded in docs/system-design.md.

risks.risk: A new message key that reaches only messages.properties fails I18nPropertiesSyncTest, which compares keys across all eleven bundles and is the enforcement REQ-LANG-002 relies on.
risks.mitigation: The page needs no new key: specialties, vets, name and none already exist in every bundle. Any key the implementer does add lands in all eleven files in the same commit.

risks.risk: Stable order is an open PRD question. An unordered render satisfies no criterion and cannot be asserted.
risks.mitigation: Narrowest reading taken: specialties by stored name from the repository query, veterinarians under each by last name then first name, ties broken by identifier. Both orderings are already the codebase's habit (PetTypeRepository, Vet.getSpecialties()).

risks.risk: The projection could drift into the controller as a stream pipeline, extending the recorded Web-controller deviation with a fresh violation that the design-validation checklist rejects outright.
risks.mitigation: The grouping is a named type with its own unit test; the controller reads two repositories, builds the projection, and returns the view name.

notes: file_targets deviation, stated for the implementer and the reviewers. The prd-entry named Specialty.java, VetRepository.java and messages.properties; this design leaves all three unchanged. Specialty needs no field, VetRepository.findAll() already serves the veterinarian side, and the page resolves from existing message keys. Two files not in file_targets are needed instead: SpecialtyRepository.java and SpecialtyDirectory.java. Open question carried forward, not blocked on: the PRD leaves the stable order unspecified, and the risks entry records the narrow reading taken. Second open question: docs/ubiquitous-language.md has no entry for 'specialty directory', which the PRD and this design both use as a term; adding it belongs to product-requirements-expert, not here. No ADR: every choice follows a pattern already in force, so the adr-template bar (a real trade-off between alternatives) is not met. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is empty.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: SpecialtyDirectory is an immutable, well-documented value object matching the codebase's Value-object pattern: List.copyOf on construction, no framework import, grouping by Specialty identifier rather than object equality (correctly averting the cross-repository identity risk the design-block flagged)

SpecialtyRepository mirrors VetRepository's javadoc, <code> tags, @Transactional(readOnly=true) and DataAccessException-throwing style exactly, and correctly omits @Cacheable since CacheConfiguration declares only the vets cache

VetController's new handler follows the existing handler shape (populate model, return view name), keeps the controller free of the grouping logic per the Web-controller pattern's no-business-rule rule, and the specialtyList.html template mirrors vetList.html's structure with every literal resolved through #{} keys
checkFormat passes; no System.out/err, no swallowed exceptions, no naming violations against architecture-principles.md

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Supply chain not verified against the NVD in this review: the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in build.gradle, and this reviewer has no network access. The slice changes no dependency, so no new exposure was introduced; closing the NVD check for the project's Spring Boot 4.1.0 / transitive stack remains a CI or human task.

SpecialtyDirectory groups by Specialty.getId(), which is null for an unpersisted Specialty. HashMap tolerates a null key so behavior stays defined, but every unsaved specialty would collapse into one bucket. Harmless on the read path under review (all instances come from the repository); worth a guard if the projection ever accepts unpersisted input.
approved_aspects: No untrusted input reaches the new route: GET /specialties.html takes no request parameter, path variable, header or body, so the slice adds no new input boundary to validate

Output escaping matches the neighboring templates: specialtyList.html renders every data value through th:text (stored specialty name, and the SpEL-concatenated vet first/last name), so a hostile stored name is escaped; no th:utext, no inline JavaScript, no remote resource, and no expression preprocessing (__${...}__) of any request- or data-derived value
No injection surface in persistence: SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties uses a constant JPQL string with no parameters and no interpolation, and is annotated @Transactional(readOnly = true)

No shell execution, file I/O, deserialization config, reflection, XML parsing, randomness, or network call is introduced; grep over the new vet sources and template found no Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec, no Files/FileWriter, no @JsonTypeInfo or enableDefaultTyping, and no /tmp usage
No credentials, tokens, or secrets in the diff; no logging is added, so no log-injection or sensitive-data-in-logs path exists

Concurrency safety over shared cached state: VetRepository.findAll is @Cacheable("vets") and returns Vet instances shared across requests, but SpecialtyDirectory only reads them — it groups into freshly allocated ArrayLists and sorts only those, and Vet.getSpecialties already returns a fresh sorted list per call, so no shared collection is mutated. The controller holds no mutable field; the projection and its SpecialtyEntry are defensively copied with List.copyOf, so the singleton controller stays stateless

Fail-secure on empty and unheld data: an empty specialty listing yields an empty entry list rather than an error, and a specialty with no holder resolves through getOrDefault(..., List.of()) rather than a null dereference

No new exposure boundary: the page discloses veterinarian and specialty names already published by the existing /vets.html and /vets routes, and the application declares no authentication or authorization to bypass

Resource use is bounded by clinic-managed lookup data, not by attacker input: findSpecialties returns the specialties table and findAll the cached vet collection, neither growable through the application (NG-2 excludes management), so the unpaged listing is not a practical DoS lever
No dependency, build-script, or configuration change in the change set: build.gradle and the Gradle files are untouched, so the slice adds no supply-chain surface

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The test name promises the acceptance criterion 'no navigation entry and no link from another page points at the page', but the body only fetches GET /specialties.html and asserts its own rendered body does not contain the literal string '/specialties.html'. That never exercises another page (vets.html, the layout fragment) for an outbound link, so the criterion it names is not actually checked — the test would still pass if a nav entry linking to /specialties.html were added to vetList.html or fragments/layout.html tomorrow. Confirmed by grep: no test in the suite renders vets.html or the layout fragment and inspects it for a specialties link.
findings.fix: Assert on a page that could plausibly carry the link instead of the specialties page itself, e.g. mockMvc.perform(get("/vets.html")).andExpect(content().string(not(containsString("/specialties.html")))) — extend to any other rendered page/fragment the nav could touch. Rename or keep the current name only if the assertion target actually matches it.

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Eight files in one module: two new vet-package classes, one new template, one new unit-test file, plus additive edits to VetController and its tests and two docs. The only edit to existing prod code is VetController gaining a constructor argument and a third handler; the /vets.html and /vets routes are untouched, and the only other construction site is the one @WebMvcTest. No build, dependency, config, schema, or seed-data change, and no sensitive path.

semantic_surprise.note: Every hunk reads as its description promises. SpecialtyDirectory groups by Specialty.getId() rather than object equality, the non-obvious right call given persisted types compare by identity and the two sides come from different reads; entry order follows the repository listing, holders sort by last name then first name then id; List.copyOf on both levels makes the projection immutable. The template resolves all four literals through message keys that already exist in every one of the ten bundles, so REQ-LANG-002 is undisturbed; data values go through th:text and are escaped; the layout menu key matches no navbar entry, so the no-navigation non-goal is honored by construction rather than by omission.

test_adequacy.note: The projection and the route are well covered by real value objects and MockMvc, and the round-2 no-inbound-link test now asserts against /vets.html with a control assertion, so it is a real fact about the page. The gap is SpecialtyRepository: its JPQL is stubbed by Mockito in every test and never runs against seeded data, so the ORDER BY specialty.name that delivers the stated stable-order acceptance criterion would survive deletion with the suite still green. The analogous lookup repository it copies, PetTypeRepository, does have a database-level test (ClinicServiceTests.shouldFindAllPetTypes), so this is a gap against the project's own precedent rather than against an absent norm.

reviewer_hedging.note: Both round-1 dissents (the missing Design link, and the tested-as-spec finding on the no-inbound-link test) were fixable-tagged, fixed, and explicitly re-verified by the same reviewers in round 2 with empty findings; code-quality and security were scoped out of the fix-delta plan, which is expected rather than silence. The residual is the security reviewer's approval-with-recommendations: SpecialtyDirectory buckets by Specialty.getId(), which is null for an unpersisted Specialty, so every unsaved specialty would collapse into one entry. Unreachable on this read path since all specialties come from the repository, but it is a caveat about code in this diff that no later round revisited. Its other recommendation, an unverified NVD supply-chain check, is a standing project condition and not about this change.

scope_deviation.note: Zero build retries, zero consultations, zero design revisions. The changed paths are exactly the design-block's primary paths, and the change touches fewer files than the PRD listed rather than more: no message-bundle key was added, and Specialty and VetRepository were left alone. Both recorded non-goals hold in the code, and the two open questions the intake left unanswered were recorded in docs/prd.md rather than silently resolved.

rationale: Correct and contained: the identity-based grouping and the no-navigation handling are the right calls, and both round-1 dissents were fixed and re-verified. Before merging, look at two things: SpecialtyRepository's ordering query is never exercised against a database, and the security reviewer's null-identifier caveat on SpecialtyDirectory was never revisited.
